events.description: * WHAT...For the Winter Weather Advisory above 6000 feet, moderate snow expected. Additional snow accumulations up to 6 inches. Wind gusts as high as 40mph. Heaviest snow is expected Wednesday morning into the afternoon, with snowfall rates 1-2+ inches per hour.

weather.description:
* WHAT...Heavy snow expected Above 5, 000 feet. Total snow
accumulations up to 31 inches. Winds gusting as high as 45 mph.

* WHERE...Sierra Nevada above 5,000 feet.

* WHEN...From 4 AM Wednesday to 4 AM PST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult to impossible. The
hazardous conditions will impact daily travel. Gusty winds could
bring down tree branches. Roads, and especially bridges and
overpasses, will likely become slick and hazardous.
weather.instruction:
If you must travel, keep an extra flashlight, food, and water in your
vehicle in case of an emergency. The latest road conditions for the
state you are calling from can be obtained by calling 5 1 1.

Persons should consider delaying all travel. If travel is absolutely
necessary, drive with extreme caution. Consider taking a winter storm
kit along with you, including such items as tire chains, booster
cables, flashlight, shovel, blankets and extra clothing. Also take
water, a first aid kit, and anything else that would help you survive
in case you become stranded.

events.title: Rip Current Statement
events.description: * WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 5 to 6 feet expected in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents expected. * WHERE...Escambia Coastal, Santa Rosa Coastal and Okaloosa Coastal Counties. * WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, from 6 AM Tuesday to midnight CST Thursday night. For the High Rip Current Risk, from 6 AM CST Tuesday through late Thursday night. * IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

location.region: Escambia Coastal; Santa Rosa Coastal; Okaloosa Coastal

weather.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 16 at 6:56PM CST until November 20 at 6:00AM CST by NWS Mobile AL
weather.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 5 to
6 feet expected in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current
Risk, dangerous rip currents expected.

* WHERE...Escambia Coastal, Santa Rosa Coastal and Okaloosa
Coastal Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, from 6 AM Tuesday to
midnight CST Thursday night. For the High Rip Current Risk,
from 6 AM CST Tuesday through late Thursday night.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
weather.instruction:
Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.
weather.areaDesc: Escambia Coastal; Santa Rosa Coastal; Okaloosa Coastal

weather.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 5
to 11 feet in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk,
dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Coastal Volusia, Coastal Indian River, Coastal Saint
Lucie, Coastal Martin, Mainland Northern Brevard, Northern
Brevard Barrier Islands, Mainland Southern Brevard and
Southern Brevard Barrier Islands Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 7 AM EST Friday. For
the High Rip Current Risk, through Thursday evening.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
weather.instruction:
High surf will affect the beaches in the advisory area, producing
localized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking
waves and dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

events.title: Winter Weather Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...Mixed precipitation expected. Ice accumulations around a light glaze to a few hundredths of an inch. For Turnagain Pass, periods of heavy snowfall expected, primarily Thursday morning, with snow totals between 7 and 10 inches. * WHERE...Anchorage and Eagle River (all elevations), Lower Matanuska Valley, SW Kenai Peninsula, NW Kenai Peninsula, Interior Kenai Peninsula, and Turnagain Pass. * WHEN...From 9 AM Wednesday to 3 AM AKST Friday. * IMPACTS...Power outages and tree damage are likely due to the ice. Travel could be nearly impossible. The hazardous conditions will impact the Wednesday evening and Thursday morning commutes. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...An atmospheric river is on track to move across the region starting Wednesday morning. Initially, the thermodynamic profile will support snow for any precipitation that overcomes strong downsloping in lee of the mountains. However, warmer air aloft moves in Wednesday afternoon as surface temperatures climb also. This will transition any light snow in lee of the mountains to a wintry mix of freezing rain and snow. As the warm nose grows in the lower levels, expect a transition to light freezing rain and then eventually to rain by Wednesday evening for the northern Cook Inlet region. This is a warmer system than the previous one, and one of the few opportunities for accumulating snow will be for Turnagain Pass, where 7 to 10 inches will most likely fall before snow transitions to mixed precipitation.

events.title: Winter Weather Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...Mixed precipitation expected. Ice accumulations around a light glaze to a few hundredths of an inch. For Turnagain Pass, periods of heavy snowfall expected, primarily Thursday morning, with snow totals between 7 and 10 inches. * WHERE...Mixed precipitation in Anchorage and Eagle River (all elevations), Lower Matanuska Valley, and NW Kenai Peninsula; heavy snowfall for Interior Kenai Peninsula and Turnagain Pass. * WHEN...From 9 AM Wednesday to 3 AM AKST Friday. * IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. The hazardous conditions will impact the Wednesday evening and Thursday morning commutes. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...This product was updated to remove SW Kenai Peninsula and correct impact information in the bullet above. An atmospheric river is on track to move across the region starting Wednesday morning. Initially, the thermodynamic profile will support snow for any precipitation that overcomes strong downsloping in lee of the mountains. However, warmer air aloft moves in Wednesday afternoon as surface temperatures climb also. This will transition any light snow in lee of the mountains to a wintry mix of freezing rain and snow. As the warm nose grows in the lower levels, expect a transition to light freezing rain and then eventually to rain by Wednesday evening for the northern Cook Inlet region. This is a warmer system than the previous one, and one of the few opportunities for accumulating snow will be for Turnagain Pass, where 7 to 10 inches will most likely fall before snow transitions to mixed precipitation.

* WHAT...Mixed precipitation expected. Ice accumulations around a
light glaze to a few hundredths of an inch. For Turnagain Pass,
periods of heavy snowfall expected, primarily Thursday morning,
with snow totals between 7 and 10 inches.

* WHERE...Mixed precipitation in Anchorage and Eagle River (all
elevations), Lower Matanuska Valley, and NW Kenai Peninsula; heavy
snowfall for Interior Kenai Peninsula and Turnagain Pass.

* WHEN...From 9 AM Wednesday to 3 AM AKST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. The hazardous conditions
will impact the Wednesday evening and Thursday morning commutes.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...This product was updated to remove SW Kenai
Peninsula and correct impact information in the bullet above. An
atmospheric river is on track to move across the region starting
Wednesday morning. Initially, the thermodynamic profile will
support snow for any precipitation that overcomes strong
downsloping in lee of the mountains. However, warmer air aloft
moves in Wednesday afternoon as surface temperatures climb also.
This will transition any light snow in lee of the mountains to a
wintry mix of freezing rain and snow. As the warm nose grows in the
lower levels, expect a transition to light freezing rain and then
eventually to rain by Wednesday evening for the northern Cook Inlet
region. This is a warmer system than the previous one, and one of
the few opportunities for accumulating snow will be for Turnagain
Pass, where 7 to 10 inches will most likely fall before snow
transitions to mixed precipitation.

For the High Surf Advisory, from 4 PM this afternoon to 4 AM PST Friday. * IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion. Large breaking waves can overpower swimmers, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks resulting in significant physical injury and increasing the risk of drowning. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without warning, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide is expected to be 1.2 ft above normal (7.0 ft MLLW) at 7:15 AM Thursday and 1.1 ft above normal (6.9 ft MLLW) at 7:45 AM Friday. These predictions include up to 1.8 ft of surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.

afternoon to 4 AM PST Friday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. Large breaking waves can overpower swimmers, pulling
people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks resulting
in significant physical injury and increasing the risk of
drowning. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without
warning, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties,
and rocks.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide
is expected to be 1.2 ft above normal (7.0 ft MLLW) at 7:15 AM
Thursday and 1.1 ft above normal (6.9 ft MLLW) at 7:45 AM Friday.
These predictions include up to 1.8 ft of surge that will
enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High tide
varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific Coast
and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.
weather.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Swimmers should remain out of the water due to dangerous surf
conditions.

Stay off of jetties, piers, rocks, and other waterside
infrastructure. Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous surf
and NEVER turn your back on the ocean. Monitor local weather,
surf and tide forecasts at www.weather.gov/mtr.

events.title: Flood Watch
events.description: * WHAT...Small stream and localized urban flooding caused by rain on snow is possible. * WHERE...Including the following area, SW Kenai Peninsula. This includes the cities of Homer, Anchor Point, Ninilchik, And Clam Gulch. * WHEN...From Wednesday morning through Thursday afternoon. * IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations. Flooding may occur in poor drainage areas. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - An atmospheric river event is anticipated to begin Wednesday morning, with ample moisture transport from the south. With upslope enhancement, most areas are on track to see 2 to 3 inches of rainfall from this system, with locally higher amounts with elevation. Heaviest rainfall rates will occur between Wednesday afternoon and Thursday morning with about a quarter of an inch per 3 hour period. This amount of rainfall on the new snowpack may cause flooding along smaller streams and creeks, in low-lying and poor drainage areas, and cause ponding of water on roadways. Rainfall is on track to decrease Thursday. - Http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

weather.headline: Flood Watch issued November 17 at 1:32PM AKST until November 19 at 6:00PM AKST by NWS Anchorage AK
weather.description:
* WHAT...Small stream and localized urban flooding caused by rain on
snow is possible.

* WHERE...Including the following area, SW Kenai Peninsula. This
includes the cities of Homer, Anchor Point, Ninilchik, And Clam
Gulch.

* WHEN...From Wednesday morning through Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- An atmospheric river event is anticipated to begin Wednesday
morning, with ample moisture transport from the south. With
upslope enhancement, most areas are on track to see 2 to 3 inches
of rainfall from this system, with locally higher amounts with
elevation. Heaviest rainfall rates will occur between Wednesday
afternoon and Thursday morning with about a quarter of an inch
per 3 hour period. This amount of rainfall on the new snowpack
may cause flooding along smaller streams and creeks, in low-lying
and poor drainage areas, and cause ponding of water on roadways.
Rainfall is on track to decrease Thursday.

- Http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
weather.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

events.title: Flood Watch
events.description: * WHAT...Small stream and localized urban flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible. * WHERE...Including the following area, Southern Kenai Mtns. This includes the city of Seward. * WHEN...From Wednesday morning through Thursday afternoon. * IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations. Storm drains and ditches may become clogged with debris. Flooding may occur in poor drainage areas. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - An atmospheric river event is anticipated to begin Wednesday morning, with ample moisture transport from the south. weather.description:
* WHAT...Heavy snow Above 5, 000 feet. Additional snow accumulations
3 to 8 inches above 5,000 feet; 1 to 3 feet above 7,000 feet. Winds
gusting as high as 50 mph along the Sierra Crest.

* WHERE...Sierra Nevada above 5,000 feet.

* WHEN...Until 4 AM PST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult to impossible. The
hazardous conditions will impact daily travel. Gusty winds could
bring down tree branches. Roads, and especially bridges and
overpasses, will likely become slick and hazardous.
weather.instruction:
If you must travel, keep an extra flashlight, food, and water in your
vehicle in case of an emergency. The latest road conditions for the
state you are calling from can be obtained by calling 5 1 1.

Persons should consider delaying all travel. If travel is absolutely
necessary, drive with extreme caution. Consider taking a winter storm
kit along with you, including such items as tire chains, booster
cables, flashlight, shovel, blankets and extra clothing. Also take
water, a first aid kit, and anything else that would help you survive
in case you become stranded.

events.title: High Wind Watch

weather.description:

weather.instruction:

direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

weather.headline: Cold Weather Advisory issued November 18 at 10:20PM PST until November 21 at 8:00AM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
weather.description:
* WHAT...Cold conditions with temperatures as low as 33 to 36 degrees
expected.

* WHERE...The East Bay.

* WHEN...From 1 AM to 8 AM PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Cold conditions will be hazardous, especially for
vulnerable populations. Prolonged exposure will lead to hypothermia
for people and animals.
weather.instruction:
Ensure portable heaters are working properly and are used correctly
to avoid sparking a fire indoors. Do not use generators or grills
inside as carbon monoxide poisoning can result.

Check with your local, city, or county officials for information on
available warming centers.

Be sure to dress in layers if outdoors. Make sure that pets and
livestock have adequate food, unfrozen water, and warmth. Cover or
tend to sensitive crops, plants, and vegetation.

events.title: High Surf Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 10- 18 feet, with local sets of 18 to 22 feet. Peak surf is expected from late tonight through Thursday night. Dangerous rip currents expected. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, moderate coastal flooding expected. * WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches. * WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 9 PM PST Friday. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 3 AM to 10 AM PST Thursday. * IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike paths, and harbor walkways. Moderate to significant beach erosion is likely. Isolated damage is unlikely but possible, especially to Pismo and Cayucos piers. There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. Breaking waves may impact the Morro Bay Harbor. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Minor coastal flooding may continue through the secondary high tide in the evening. Additional hazardous surf and coastal flooding issues are expected next week.

location.region: San Luis Obispo County Beaches; Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches

weather.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 18 at 7:01PM PST until November 20 at 9:00PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
weather.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 10-
18 feet, with local sets of 18 to 22 feet. Peak surf is
expected from late tonight through Thursday night. Dangerous
rip currents expected. For the Coastal Flood Advisory,
moderate coastal flooding expected.

* WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara
County Central Coast Beaches.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 9 PM PST Friday. For
the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 3 AM to 10 AM PST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some
vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time
of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike paths,
and harbor walkways. Moderate to significant beach erosion is
likely. Isolated damage is unlikely but possible, especially
to Pismo and Cayucos piers. There is an increased risk for
ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers out
to sea. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off
beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore.
Breaking waves may impact the Morro Bay Harbor.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Minor coastal flooding may continue through
the secondary high tide in the evening. Additional hazardous
surf and coastal flooding issues are expected next week.
weather.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. Do
NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

Remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions, or stay
near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in
such conditions, stay off the rocks.
weather.areaDesc: San Luis Obispo County Beaches; Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches

flood levels through late week and into this weekend.

events.title: Flood Warning
events.description: ...Forecast flooding changed from Moderate to Major severity for the following rivers in Florida... St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties. .On the St Johns River at Astor, the river is forecast to continue to rise through Moderate Flood Stage, reaching Major Flood Stage into early next week due to strong onshore flow causing a surge up the river as well as additional heavy rainfall expected across the basin. For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Major flooding is forecast. * WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast. * WHERE...St Johns River near Astor. * WHEN...Until further notice. * IMPACTS...At 4.0 feet, Major flooding occurs with water entering many structures on canals and along the river. Long duration flooding will occur, with levels taking weeks to months to return below flood stage. Water rescues will be necessary. River Road becomes inaccessible, with 1 to 2 feet water depth in numerous homes on Wildhog, Possum, Bonnet and Snail roads. Roads along Blue Creek are inaccessible with major flooding of homes on Otter, Branch and Chestnut roads. Camp South Moon Road and Juno Trail are inaccessible. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 8:30 AM EST Thursday the stage was 3.2 feet. - Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet. - Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending at 8:30 AM EST Thursday was 3.2 feet. - Forecast...The river is expected to rise to 4.0 feet Monday morning. Additional rises are possible thereafter. - Flood stage is 2.3 feet. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 15 to 18 ft. * WHERE...San Francisco County. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 10 AM PST Friday. For the High Surf Advisory until 1 AM PST Friday. * IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion. Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas. Large breaking waves can overpower swimmers, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks resulting in significant physical injury and increasing the risk of drowning. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide is expected to be 1.2 ft above normal (7.0 ft MLLW) at 7:15 AM Thursday and 1.1 ft above normal (6.9 ft MLLW) at 7:45 AM Friday. These predictions include up to 1.8 ft of surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.

events.title: Flood Watch
events.description: * WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible. * WHERE...Most of east central Florida, including Volusia, Seminole, Orange, Osceola, Okeechobee, Brevard, Indian River, Saint Lucie, and Martin counties. * WHEN...From Tuesday afternoon through Friday evening. * IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - Repeated rounds of showers and isolated storms are forecast through Friday. Rainfall amounts of 3 to 6 inches are forecast with localized higher amounts of 8 to 12 inches. The greatest potential for these higher amounts will be over the coastal counties. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

weather.headline: Flood Watch issued November 16 at 3:18PM EST until November 20 at 7:00PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
weather.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...Most of east central Florida, including Volusia, Seminole,
Orange, Osceola, Okeechobee, Brevard, Indian River, Saint Lucie,
and Martin counties.

* WHEN...From Tuesday afternoon through Friday evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Repeated rounds of showers and isolated storms are forecast
through Friday. Rainfall amounts of 3 to 6 inches are forecast
with localized higher amounts of 8 to 12 inches. The greatest
potential for these higher amounts will be over the coastal
counties.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
weather.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

events.title: Flood Warning
events.description: * WHAT...Flooding caused by upstream dam release continues. * WHERE...Maricopa County in south central Arizona... Northeastern Yuma County in southwestern Arizona... * WHEN...Until 1100 AM MST Tuesday Nov 24. * IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations is expected. Low-water crossings are likely to become inundated with water and may not be passable. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 815 AM MST, water releases from Painted Rock Dam continue with flow peaking around 3000 cfs. A streamflow gauge immediately downstream also indicated a stage near 10 feet. - Flooding is expected along the Gila River. - Some locations that will experience flooding include... Farmlands and low-water crossings along the Gila River. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

location.region: Maricopa, AZ; Yuma, AZ

weather.headline: Flood Warning issued November 17 at 8:21AM MST until November 24 at 11:00AM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
weather.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by upstream dam release continues.

* WHERE...Maricopa County in south central Arizona...
Northeastern Yuma County in southwestern Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 1100 AM MST Tuesday Nov 24.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is expected. Low-water crossings are
likely to become inundated with water and may not be passable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 815 AM MST, water releases from Painted Rock Dam continue with
flow peaking around 3000 cfs. A streamflow gauge immediately
downstream also indicated a stage near 10 feet.
- Flooding is expected along the Gila River.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Farmlands and low-water crossings along the Gila River.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
weather.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

weather.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 5

dangerous rip currents and rough surf.

* WHERE...Coastal Volusia, Coastal Indian River, Coastal Saint
Lucie, Coastal Martin, Mainland Northern Brevard, Northern
Brevard Barrier Islands, Mainland Southern Brevard and
Southern Brevard Barrier Islands Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 7 PM EST Saturday.
For the High Rip Current Risk, through Saturday evening.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
weather.instruction:
High surf will affect the beaches in the advisory area, producing
localized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking
waves and dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

weather.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 19 at 11:56AM CST until November 20 at 12:00AM CST by NWS Mobile AL
weather.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 4 to
6 feet in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk,
dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...In Alabama, Mobile Coastal and Baldwin Coastal
Counties. In Florida, Escambia Coastal, Santa Rosa Coastal and
Okaloosa Coastal Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until midnight CST tonight.
For the High Rip Current Risk, through Saturday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and

weather.instruction:
Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

* IMPACTS...Winter driving conditions are expected. Roads, and

weather.instruction:
If you must travel, keep an extra flashlight, food, and water in your
vehicle in case of an emergency. For winter road conditions from the
Utah Department of Transportation, visit
http://www.udottraffic.utah.gov.

Persons should delay all travel if possible. If travel is absolutely
necessary, drive with extreme caution and be prepared for sudden
changes in visibility. Leave plenty of room between you and the
motorist ahead of you, and allow extra time to reach your
destination. Avoid sudden braking or acceleration, and be especially
cautious on hills or when making turns. Make sure your car is
winterized and in good working order.

NWS Forecast, High End Amount, and Low End Amount, visit
weather.gov/slc/winter.

weather.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

BACKCOUNTRY AVALANCHE WARNING IMMEDIATE BROADCAST REQUESTED 05:30 PST Thu Nov 19 2026 The Sierra Avalanche Center in Truckee has issued a BACKCOUNTRY AVALANCHE WARNING for the following areas: NWS Reno NV - NVZ002 (Greater Lake Tahoe)...CAZ072 (Greater Lake Tahoe (CA)) * WHAT...HIGH avalanche danger exists in the backcountry. Large avalanches are expected across backcountry terrain. * WHERE...Central Sierra Nevada Mountains between Yuba Pass (Hwy 49) on the north and Ebbetts Pass (Hwy 4) on the south, including the greater Lake Tahoe area. This applies only to backcountry areas, not to ski areas and highways where avalanche mitigation programs exist. * WHEN...In effect from Thu 05:30 PST to Fri 04:00 PST. * IMPACTS...Significant amounts of new snow and wind are creating dangerous avalanche conditions in the backcountry. The new snow is overloading a weak snowpack in some upper elevation areas. Avalanches could run down into treed terrain. * PRECAUTIONARY / PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS...Very dangerous avalanche conditions exist in the backcountry. Traveling in, near, or below backcountry avalanche terrain is not recommended during HIGH avalanche danger. Consult https://www.sierraavalanchecenter.org/ or www.avalanche.org for more detailed information. Similar avalanche danger may exist at locations outside the coverage area of this or any avalanche center.

weather.description:
* WHAT...Heavy snow Above 5,000 feet. Additional snow accumulations 3
to 8 inches above 5,000 feet; 1 to 3 feet above 7,000 feet. Winds
gusting as high as 50 mph along the Sierra Crest.

* WHERE...Sierra Nevada above 5,000 feet.

* WHEN...Until 4 AM PST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult to impossible. The
hazardous conditions will impact daily travel. Gusty winds could
bring down tree branches. Roads, and especially bridges and
overpasses, will likely become slick and hazardous.
weather.instruction:
If you must travel, keep an extra flashlight, food, and water in your
vehicle in case of an emergency. The latest road conditions for the
state you are calling from can be obtained by calling 5 1 1.

Persons should consider delaying all travel. If travel is absolutely
necessary, drive with extreme caution. Consider taking a winter storm
kit along with you, including such items as tire chains, booster
cables, flashlight, shovel, blankets and extra clothing. Also take
water, a first aid kit, and anything else that would help you survive
in case you become stranded.

events.title: Coastal Flood Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding. For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents. * WHERE...Kenedy Island, Willacy Island and Cameron Island Counties. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 6 PM CST Friday. For the High Rip Current Risk, through Friday afternoon. * IMPACTS...Nuisance flooding is expected, with water reaching or pushing into the dunes on South Padre Island. Vehicles, except those with four wheel drive and high wheel bases, will be unable to be driven on the beach. This includes locations north of Public Beach Access #3. Minor to moderate beach erosion is expected. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

location.region: Kenedy Island; Willacy Island; Cameron Island

weather.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 19 at 6:02PM CST until November 20 at 6:00PM CST by NWS Brownsville TX
weather.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding.
For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Kenedy Island, Willacy Island and Cameron Island
Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 6 PM CST Friday.
For the High Rip Current Risk, through Friday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Nuisance flooding is expected, with water reaching or
pushing into the dunes on South Padre Island. Vehicles, except
those with four wheel drive and high wheel bases, will be unable
to be driven on the beach. This includes locations north of
Public Beach Access #3. Minor to moderate beach erosion is
expected. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
weather.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.
weather.areaDesc: Kenedy Island; Willacy Island; Cameron Island

Point MacKenzie and Big Lake with bands of moderate to heavy snow
expected by early evening. Snowfall rates of 1 to 2 inches per hour
are possible during this time. The heavy snow is expected to move
northeast across the Lower matanuska Valley through this evening
with rain changing to snow for Wasilla and Palmer by around 5 PM.
Any heavy snow may lead to rapid accumulations on area roadways as
well as significantly reduced visibilities. Snow is expected to
taper off from southwest to northeast tonight.

conditions call 5 1 1 or visit 511.alaska.gov.

weather.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 6

shore and call or wave for help.
